title: Bhawana Kanth Becomes India's First Woman 'Top Gun' After Completing Elite Combat Course
excerpt: Squadron Leader Kanth has completed the prestigious Fighter Combat Leader course at TACDE in Gwalior, joining the IAF's finest combat tacticians in a decade of firsts.
body:
• Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth has become the first woman to complete the Fighter Combat Leader (FCL) course at TACDE in Gwalior
  • The FCL course, India's equivalent of the American 'Top Gun' school, selects roughly one in every hundred fighter pilots
  • Kanth was part of the IAF's first batch of women fighter pilots in 2016 and became the first woman qualified for combat missions in 2019
  • She has transitioned from flying the MiG-21 Bison to the Su-30 MKI, one of India's most capable frontline fighters

Squadron Leader Bhawana Kanth has earned the distinction of being the first woman officer in the Indian Air Force to complete the Fighter Combat Leader (FCL) course at the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment (TACDE) in Gwalior — an achievement often compared to graduating from America's legendary Top Gun school.

The Toughest Badge in the IAF

The FCL course is considered one of the most demanding qualifications a fighter pilot can earn in the Indian Air Force. Conducted over nearly 20 weeks, it selects a tiny fraction of the Air Force's fighter pilots, with reports suggesting roughly one in every hundred aircrew is chosen.

Pilots undergo rigorous training in advanced air combat tactics, weapons employment, electronic warfare, combat maneuvering, and operational leadership. Graduates return to their squadrons as tactical experts responsible for shaping combat strategies and mentoring fellow fighter pilots.

"Each breakthrough expands the aperture for women in combat aviation — and Kanth's Top Gun badge pushes that frontier to its highest point yet."

TACDE has been the IAF's premier tactical training institution since the early 1970s, developing combat doctrines and evaluating new aircraft and weapon systems. Its instructors are handpicked from among the Air Force's best.

A Decade of Breaking Barriers

Kanth's latest milestone caps a decade of firsts. In June 2016, she became one of the IAF's first three women fighter pilots alongside Avani Chaturvedi and Mohana Singh, after India opened the fighter stream to women. In 2019, she became the first Indian woman fighter pilot cleared to undertake combat missions by day on the MiG-21 Bison.

She later transitioned to the Su-30 MKI, one of India's most capable frontline fighter aircraft, and was awarded the Nari Shakti Puraskar in 2020, India's highest civilian honor for women.

Originally from Darbhanga, Bihar, Kanth trained as an engineer at BMS College of Engineering in Bangalore and was recruited by Tata Consultancy Services in 2014 before pursuing her dream of military aviation through the UPSC Combined Defence Services examination.

Women Reshaping the IAF

Kanth's achievement is part of a broader transformation within the Indian Air Force. Women first entered the IAF cockpit in 1994 when Flight Lieutenant Harita Kaur Deol became the first woman to fly solo. For more than two decades, women were limited to transport aircraft and helicopters until the fighter stream opened in 2016.

Since then, Mohana Singh became the first woman to fly the indigenous LCA Tejas in a frontline squadron. Shivangi Singh earned the Qualified Flying Instructor badge and flew President Droupadi Murmu in a Rafale fighter. Earlier this year, Squadron Leader Saanya became the first woman to secure the Category-A Qualified Flying Instructor qualification.

Each breakthrough expands the aperture for women in combat aviation — and Kanth's Top Gun badge pushes that frontier to its highest point yet.
nri_angle: Kanth's achievement resonates as a powerful symbol of India's progress on gender equality in defense, inspiring diaspora families and their children with a story of breaking barriers in one of the world's most demanding professions.
author: Diaspora Desk
